title: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists

tasks.short: Evaluate jobs, assign grades and recommend salary and applicable working-time coverage.

steps.what: Receive the job evaluation request and gather the current role description and organisation context.
Interview the line manager and job holder to establish actual duties and responsibilities.
Organise evidence by evaluation factor and identify missing or contradictory information.

loop.input: Job description, interview notes and approved evaluation-factor definitions.
loop.output: Evidence table containing source passages, factor labels and unresolved gaps.
loop.check: Verify quotations and source locations; specialist checks placement and completeness. No inferred duties or scores.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt per job; unresolved gaps return for human clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevant duties appear in varied prose and interview notes, so fixed field mappings are insufficient.

steps.what: Determine collective-agreement and working-time coverage under the applicable national rules.
Rate evaluation factors and compare the job with established benchmark roles.
Challenge the evaluation and approve the grade and coverage assessment.
Recommend a salary range or salary using approved bands and relevant market comparisons.
Approve the salary recommendation or refer an exception to the authorised decision maker.
Record approved classification and salary decisions, then notify the requesting manager.

tasks.design: Configure job intake and decision records in the {WORKFLOW} and {HCM}, with evidence retained in the {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop organises source passages for specialist evaluation; deterministic calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} produce salary-band comparisons in the {BI}. Separate classification and salary approvals unlock record updates and notifications.
tasks.previous_blocker: Role descriptions used inconsistent language, evidence was dispersed, and factor ratings depended on tacit calibration between evaluators.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can organise prose without deciding the grade. AI-assisted coding makes evidence tables, comparison calculations and approval links cheaper to implement.
tasks.still_hard: Actual duties may differ from written descriptions, and contested grading requires careful calibration. There is no universal European exempt/non-exempt split: coverage follows national rules and collective agreements. GDPR applies, and AI used to evaluate workers or affect employment terms needs an AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish the value of a job from the influence of its holder or manager, and explain a defensible comparison.

ambition.what: An early job-design consultation for managers before a new role is approved.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less evidence sorting and record entry, with more time for interviews, calibration and job-design advice. The specialist can offer earlier classification advice; binding grade and salary decisions retain their explicit approval routes.

reach.task: Review whether job evaluation factors disadvantage comparable groups.
reach.learn: Gender-neutral factor definitions, comparator selection and bias in job descriptions.

reach.task: Design roles and reporting structures before recruitment.
reach.learn: Organisation design, responsibility boundaries and how role changes affect grading.

evidence.claim: Evidence extraction, factor-score arithmetic and salary-band comparisons can be separated from human classification decisions.
Job or worker evaluation that affects employment terms needs assessment against the AI Act employment category.
GDPR Article 22 is relevant if classification or salary decisions become solely automated with significant effects.
The digest identifies gender-neutral job evaluation as a pay-transparency requirement; national implementation needs checking.

assumptions: An approved job evaluation framework and benchmark roles already exist.
The pilot covers one national jurisdiction and job family.
Market pay data is licensed for the proposed use.
The loop extracts evidence only; it does not rate workers or assign grades.
The judgement-heavy prior is retained; gains chiefly come from preparation, comparisons and recording.
Build ranges include applicable consultation and access work; external waiting may extend rollout.
unknowns: Which evaluation framework, collective agreements and national rules apply.
How consistently evaluators currently rate the same job evidence.
Whether benchmark jobs and salary bands are current and approved.
Which classification and salary decisions require additional approval or an appeal route.
research_questions: Can evaluators reproduce factor ratings when given the same evidence table?
Which national provisions determine working-time and collective-agreement coverage?
Does the intended extraction-only use fall within the relevant AI Act category?
new_work: Check extracted evidence and resolve missing duties.
Maintain benchmark roles and salary-band data.
Calibrate evaluators and review contested classifications.
Monitor whether evidence extraction systematically omits particular kinds of work.
Maintain decision records and handle appeals.
tasks.statement: Evaluate job positions, determining classification, exempt or non-exempt status, and salary.

tasks.short: Maintain compensation and benefits compliance with EU and national rules, including required reporting.

steps.what: Review regulatory notices, reporting calendars and collective agreement changes.

loop.input: Approved regulatory notices and agreement changes with jurisdiction and publication metadata.
loop.output: Candidate obligations with exact source passages, dates and affected topics.
loop.check: Validate source passages and dates mechanically; a specialist checks scope and omissions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; missing sources or ambiguity go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Notices express changes in prose and use inconsistent structures; extraction does not decide applicability.

steps.what: Determine applicable obligations, interpretations, owners and deadlines.
Extract employee, pay and benefit data for required checks.
Reconcile totals, test required fields and investigate discrepancies.
Prepare required reports and assemble supporting evidence.
Review exceptions and approve the report for submission.
File the approved report and retain the official receipt.

tasks.design: Maintain approved obligations, owners and deadlines in the {WORKFLOW}; a bounded extraction loop proposes changes from controlled documents in the {DOCS}. Scheduled {DATA_PLATFORM} checks reconcile {HCM} and {PAYROLL} data and generate reports with evidence, while the approved release is submitted through the {GOV_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applicability requires legal interpretation, while evidence is spread across systems. Reporting formats and national rules change.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable validation code and report templates reduce preparation work. Bounded extraction can surface source-backed changes for review without deciding their legal effect.
tasks.still_hard: Legal interpretation, collective agreements and incomplete historical records remain difficult. GDPR, the EU AI Act and national reporting and consultation rules need separate applicability checks.
tasks.human_edge: Judge materiality, resolve competing interpretations and take responsibility for what the company declares.

ambition.what: Monthly compensation and benefits reporting readiness decisions

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more time resolving control failures before deadlines and less time assembling reports. They can recommend remediation priorities; legal interpretation and filing approval retain their existing owners.

reach.task: Assess whether job evaluation and pay reporting categories are defensible.
reach.learn: Gender-neutral evaluation criteria, comparison groups and limits of pay-gap statistics.

evidence.claim: Obligation registers, scheduled controls and template reporting are established deterministic patterns; this design is unvalidated.
AI used for specified employment decisions may fall within Annex III; intended use needs assessment.
The digest identifies gender-neutral job evaluation as relevant to pay transparency.
The digest documents Dutch works council consent requirements for specified HR data and monitoring arrangements.

assumptions: The first release covers a defined reporting obligation in one jurisdiction.
A legal adviser approves interpretation before executable checks change.
Reports have stable templates; unresolved narrative explanations remain human-authored.
Estimates include applicable national consultation work, access and a parallel reporting rehearsal.
unknowns: Which entities, jurisdictions, agreements and reporting obligations are in scope?
Which data definitions and control totals are authoritative?
Who can approve interpretations and release filings?
Which consultation, retention and data-access requirements apply to this employer?
research_questions: Which obligations can be tested completely from existing records?
Which reporting specifications support schema validation before submission?
new_work: Review extracted changes and maintain the obligation register.
Version approved interpretations and executable controls.
Investigate failed checks and document accepted exceptions.
Maintain report templates and verify filing receipts.
tasks.statement: Ensure company compliance with federal and state laws, including reporting requirements.

tasks.short: Advise employees and managers on employment rules, agreements, compensation, benefits and job classification.

steps.what: Read an employee or manager request and identify its topic.
Clarify relevant facts, jurisdiction, agreement and the employee's concern.
Find current policies, agreement clauses and relevant employee records.
Interpret the sources and resolve conflicts or seek specialist advice.
Draft an explanation of the advice and available next steps.

loop.input: The specialist's advice position, relevant case facts and current source passages.
loop.output: A plain-language response with source references, assumptions and next steps.
loop.check: Check source versions, figures and references; specialist verifies that the draft preserves their interpretation.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing sources or contradictions return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Case-specific explanations require prose; fixed templates can cover only standard questions.

steps.what: Explain the advice and discuss consequences with the employee or manager.
Record the advice, source versions and follow-up commitments.

tasks.design: Configure structured intake and case records in the {HELPDESK}, with permission-filtered retrieval from the {DOCS} and {HCM}. A bounded loop drafts explanations from the specialist's advice position and cited sources; the specialist approves delivery, while the {WORKFLOW} records approved advice and schedules agreed follow-ups.
tasks.previous_blocker: Answers depend on jurisdiction, agreement versions and individual circumstances. Search and case records often lack consistent metadata.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured intake and versioned retrieval can remove repeated searches. Bounded drafting turns an approved interpretation into a clearer explanation.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting agreements, disputed facts and sensitive conversations require a person. Retrieval cannot establish that a source legally governs a case.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the concern behind the question, explain difficult outcomes and recognise when legal or labour relations advice is needed.

ambition.what: Guided comparisons of benefit options before employee life changes

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time locating clauses and writing repeated explanations, leaving more time for complex advice. They can offer guided scenario sessions; authority over employment terms remains unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare an agreement interpretation brief for a disputed compensation question.
reach.learn: Agreement hierarchy, consultation routes and how to document competing interpretations.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, controlled retrieval and reviewed drafting are feasible support patterns; no directly matching product case is supplied.
Advice tooling should be assessed separately if its outputs determine significant employment outcomes.
Employment decision support may require assessment against Annex III depending on intended use.

assumptions: The proposed service assists a specialist and does not decide pay, classification or benefit entitlement.
Intake uses selectable topics and routes unclassified requests to a person.
Policies and agreements have identifiable owners, versions and effective dates.
Case logging uses approved text and structured follow-up fields rather than automatic call recording.
Estimates include permission testing and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Is advice currently recorded in a case system, employee record or shared mailbox?
Which policies and agreements are approved and reliably versioned?
Which questions require legal review before an answer is delivered?
Who may access individual advice records, and for how long?
research_questions: Can retrieval reliably filter by jurisdiction, agreement coverage and effective date?
Which recurring questions are fully answerable with approved templates?
How should the service detect missing facts before drafting?
new_work: Maintain source versions, coverage metadata and permissions.
Review drafts and resolve missing or conflicting sources.
Record agreed next steps in structured fields.
Review recurring unanswered questions and improve approved guidance.
tasks.statement: Advise managers and employees on state and federal employment regulations, collective agreements, benefit and compensation policies, personnel procedures, and classification programs.

tasks.short: Develop, test and communicate fair methods for selection, progression, pay, evaluation and training.

steps.what: Retrieve workforce records and existing method documentation for the review.
Compare outcomes, costs and process weaknesses using an analysis workbook.
Draft revised criteria, procedures and implementation options.

loop.input: Approved methods, job evidence, research brief, baseline measures and a proposal template.
loop.output: A method proposal with traceable criteria, implementation options and open questions.
loop.check: Verify references and required sections; the specialist checks fairness, relevance and unsupported assumptions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per proposal; unsupported points remain explicit questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates structure the proposal, but explaining choices requires synthesis of contextual evidence.

steps.what: Consult managers and employee representatives, then agree a bounded pilot.
Calculate pilot results, projected costs and differences against agreed criteria.
Judge pilot findings and approve the method and implementation limits.
Publish approved guidance and notify affected managers.

tasks.design: A deterministic pipeline combines approved extracts from the {HCM} and process outcome datasets in the {DATA_PLATFORM}, then produces baseline and pilot comparisons in the {BI}. A bounded loop drafts proposals in the {DOCS}; consultation and approval control pilot launch and method adoption, followed by configured publication through the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Outcome definitions differed across HR processes, while methods mixed policy, judgement and local practice. Automating publication alone did little to improve method quality.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable calculations and versioned templates make comparisons repeatable. AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort, while bounded drafting prepares proposals from approved evidence.
tasks.still_hard: A pilot may be small or biased. Choosing defensible criteria, interpreting unequal outcomes and agreeing changes remain substantive work.
tasks.human_edge: Choose criteria that reflect real work, challenge misleading averages and negotiate methods that managers and employees can use fairly.

ambition.what: Quarterly decisions on whether promotion criteria need revision, supported by outcome and cost comparisons.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more time designing pilots and interpreting outcomes. With delegated pilot authority, they can test procedural changes within agreed limits; employment and pay decisions retain their designated approvers.

reach.task: Test whether training requirements support progression.
reach.learn: Define measurable learning outcomes and separate course completion from demonstrated capability.

reach.task: Review differences in selection and progression outcomes.
reach.learn: Assess comparator quality, small samples and plausible explanations without treating correlations as findings.

evidence.claim: Deterministic outcome comparisons and bounded proposal drafting are plausible; the digest supplies no direct case for this task.
AI used for recruitment or worker evaluation requires an EU AI Act classification assessment.
A human approval label alone does not resolve significant automated decision concerns when a score determines the outcome.

assumptions: Time shares cover a review cycle, including manager approval; operational pilot delivery belongs to the relevant HR process.
Existing outcome extracts can be reused; access to the {ATS}, {TALENT} or {LMS} is added only when needed.
The loop drafts methods and does not rank people or recommend individual employment decisions.
Build ranges cover one method family and one pilot, including access, testing and applicable national consultation.
GDPR and EU AI Act scope are assessed before personal outcome data or AI-supported evaluation is introduced.
unknowns: Which method family is the initial priority.
Availability and comparability of selection, promotion, compensation, evaluation and training outcomes.
Existing collective agreements and applicable national consultation requirements.
Pilot authority, approval rights and acceptable implementation limits.
Permitted analysis of sensitive personal data and minimum reporting group sizes.
research_questions: Which outcome measures distinguish a method improvement from changes in the participating population?
Can available process exports support valid comparisons across review periods?
new_work: Maintain measure definitions and calculation versions.
Review draft proposals and verify their sources.
Monitor pilots for unintended effects and incomplete participation.
Keep method versions, consultation records and implementation limits aligned.
Assess changes in legal scope when the solution's purpose expands.
tasks.statement: Plan, develop, evaluate, improve, and communicate methods and techniques for selecting, promoting, compensating, evaluating, and training workers.

tasks.short: Advise on classification and salary complaints using job evidence, pay rules and employee discussions.

steps.what: Receive the complaint and clarify the requested outcome.
Retrieve job profiles, pay history and applicable classification rules.
Compare disputed duties and salary treatment with documented criteria and relevant precedents.

loop.input: Access-filtered complaint evidence pack and approved precedents.
loop.output: Criterion-by-criterion comparison with quotations, references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check source references and figures automatically; specialist verifies relevance and missing evidence.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair; unresolved comparisons return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Descriptions of actual duties and complaint narratives require contextual reading.

steps.what: Discuss actual duties, disputed facts and concerns with the employee and manager.
Form a recommendation explaining classification, salary treatment and possible remedies.
Approve the advice and any proposed remedy within delegated authority.
Record the approved advice, evidence references and follow-up responsibility.
Send the approved written advice to the agreed recipients.

tasks.design: Configure restricted complaint intake in the {WORKFLOW} and retrieve evidence from the {HCM}, {PAYROLL} and {DOCS}. A bounded reading loop drafts a referenced comparison; specialists conduct discussions and formulate advice, while the HR manager approves the response. The {WORKFLOW} records and sends that exact approved version through the {HCM} and {EMAIL}, without changing pay.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence spans several systems, and similar job titles can conceal materially different duties. Rules alone cannot resolve contested facts or fairness concerns.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and integrations can assemble case packs. Bounded text extraction can prepare comparisons from approved sources.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed duties, inconsistent precedents and interpretation of collective agreements require expert judgement. GDPR, EU AI Act applicability and national rules require assessment before using models in employment decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Listen without prejudging the complaint, establish credible facts and explain a defensible recommendation.

ambition.what: Pre-complaint classification clarification clinic

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time locating evidence and more time discussing disputed duties. They can offer early classification consultations within the approved framework; pay and grade changes require existing delegated approvals.

reach.task: Prepare grievance resolution options.
reach.learn: Collective-agreement interpretation, representation rights and escalation procedures.

reach.task: Check the implementation of an approved salary correction.
reach.learn: Effective dates, retrospective calculations and payroll cutoffs.

evidence.claim: Restricted case intake, evidence retrieval and approved-response routing are established deterministic patterns; this design is an estimate.
The human decision boundary reflects the potential significant effects of salary decisions; Article 22 applicability depends on the actual process.
Model use in worker evaluation or employment decisions needs an intended-use assessment against the EU AI Act.

assumptions: The baseline describes a typical mid-size employer; time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
Salary and classification advice remains a substantive human judgement despite the task's automation prior.
Consent and access work includes privacy review, access approval and employee consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Where complaint records and precedents are held today.
Which classification framework and collective agreements apply.
Who can approve advice, remedies and salary changes.
Whether permitted interfaces expose historical pay and job records.
research_questions: Which national complaint, representation and consultation rules apply?
Does the proposed model use fall within regulated employment AI?
How reliably can evidence extraction distinguish actual duties from job-title assumptions?
new_work: Verify extracted comparisons and irrelevant precedents.
Resolve missing records and conflicting effective dates.
Maintain access filters, retention rules and approved precedent versions.
Check that sent advice matches the approved version.
tasks.statement: Provide advice on the resolution of classification and salary complaints.

tasks.short: Prepare job classifications, job descriptions and salary scales.

steps.what: Retrieve the job request, position records and existing classification.
Collect relevant benchmark tables and approved evaluation guidance.
Interview the manager and job holder about responsibilities, scope and working conditions.
Write the job description using confirmed job facts and standard sections.

loop.input: Confirmed job facts, interview notes and approved description template.
loop.output: Draft description with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate required sections; the specialist checks factual support and gender-neutral wording.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing or conflicting facts return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cannot reliably turn varied interview notes into clear, faithful descriptions.

steps.what: Evaluate job factors and recommend a classification using the approved framework.
Calculate proposed salary ranges and check internal relativities and benchmark fit.
Approve the description, classification and salary scales after resolving exceptions.
Publish approved descriptions and update effective-dated classifications and salary scales.

tasks.design: An integration reads position records from the {HCM} and assembles licensed benchmarks and approved guidance from the {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop prepares descriptions, while deterministic calculations produce salary ranges and exception checks; specialists evaluate jobs and the manager approves changes. The {WORKFLOW} then publishes only the approved versions to the {HCM} and {DOCS}, with effective dates and an audit trail.
tasks.previous_blocker: Job facts, benchmark licences and evaluation frameworks differ. Standard forms reduce typing but do not resolve contested job scope.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding can reduce the effort of building adapters, calculation tools and document generation. Bounded drafting can turn confirmed notes into a consistent description.
tasks.still_hard: Benchmark matching and gender-neutral factor interpretation need expertise. Assess GDPR and EU AI Act obligations if the tool influences employment decisions; human approval alone does not settle that assessment. National consultation rules vary.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish the job's actual scope from an inflated title, challenge inconsistent evaluations and explain difficult pay relativities.

ambition.what: Pre-recruitment job scope and pay-range clinic for hiring managers.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling descriptions and more time resolving disputed job scope. A delegated right to approve routine description corrections could be added; grade and pay authority remains with the manager unless explicitly changed.

reach.task: Translate a planned vacancy into an accurate role brief.
reach.learn: Structured job interviews, vacancy requirements and how role scope affects recruitment.

reach.task: Check effective-dated salary scale changes before payroll processing.
reach.learn: Pay element mapping, effective dates and retrospective adjustment rules.

evidence.claim: Structured job records, controlled templates and deterministic range calculations can support this workflow; no compensation-specific implementation is documented in the digest.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: The company has an approved job evaluation framework and reusable description templates.
Benchmark use and derived outputs remain within the data licence.
The tool does not autonomously grade jobs or change employee pay.
Estimates cover a controlled pilot with one job framework and one principal {HCM}; consultation time is elapsed working days.
The structured-input prior fits records and calculations, but interviews and factor judgement remain substantial.
unknowns: Which evaluation framework, collective agreements and benchmark licences apply?
Can the {HCM} accept effective-dated framework changes through approved interfaces?
Who can approve classification changes and salary scales?
Which employee consultation requirements apply under national rules?
research_questions: What validation is appropriate for gender-neutral evaluation factors in the relevant jurisdiction?
Would the intended use place any model component within EU AI Act employment provisions?
new_work: Review generated descriptions against source notes.
Resolve incomplete job facts and benchmark mismatches.
Maintain calculation rules, templates and benchmark versions.
Check publication failures, effective dates and access permissions.
tasks.statement: Prepare occupational classifications, job descriptions, and salary scales.

tasks.short: Maintain personnel records and keep employee handbooks current.

steps.what: Receive approved personnel changes and policy revisions through forms and the shared mailbox.
Check employee identity, effective dates, approvals and required fields against existing records.
Update personnel fields and file approved supporting documents.
Identify handbook sections affected by the approved policy revision.

loop.input: Approved policy revision and current employee handbook.
loop.output: Affected sections with quoted source passages and proposed change scope.
loop.check: Verify section identifiers and quotations; specialist checks omitted cross-references.
loop.stop: One pass and one correction attempt per revision; uncertain scope returns to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword search misses paraphrases and policy dependencies across free-text sections.

steps.what: Draft handbook amendments and assemble the revised version.

loop.input: Reviewed handbook change map, approved policy and handbook template.
loop.output: Handbook draft with tracked amendments and source references.
loop.check: Check unchanged sections, dates and references; specialist reviews obligations and wording.
loop.stop: One draft and two revision attempts; unresolved contradictions remain flagged for human editing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Document assembly is deterministic, but coherent amendments require reading and rewriting policy prose.

steps.what: Approve the handbook revision after required legal review and employee consultation.
Publish the approved handbook, archive the superseded version and request acknowledgements where needed.
Compare record changes and handbook acknowledgements with outstanding requests.

tasks.design: Configure structured change requests and validation in the {WORKFLOW} and {HCM}, with approved documents retained in the {DOCS}. A bounded reading and drafting loop prepares handbook amendments for an HR manager's approval; configured publication then distributes that approved version. A reconciliation job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} feeds outstanding changes and acknowledgements to the {BI}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes arrived in inconsistent messages, approval evidence was scattered, and handbook cross-references required manual reading.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record workflows can enforce required fields and approval references. Small integrations and bounded document loops are cheaper to build and maintain with AI-assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting effective dates, retention rules and policy changes remain difficult. GDPR and national consultation rules apply; handbook acknowledgement does not establish consent to contractual changes.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparently clerical update changes an employee's rights or needs explanation.

ambition.what: A dated policy-change summary showing employees which handbook sections changed.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from copying records and formatting documents to resolving exceptions and explaining policy changes. The specialist can manage the approved revision schedule; authority to change employment terms remains with the authorised decision makers.

reach.task: Manage effective-dated records and document retention.
reach.learn: Record provenance, access permissions and correction procedures.

reach.task: Prepare consultation material for handbook changes.
reach.learn: Which changes require consultation and what evidence must be retained.

evidence.claim: Structured record updates, version control and exception reconciliation are established deterministic capabilities.
Bounded drafting can prepare handbook amendments; it does not establish their legal validity.
In the Netherlands, some HR data and monitoring arrangements require works council consent; other countries need a national assessment.

assumptions: Personnel changes already carry the required substantive approval before record entry.
Routine updates use structured forms; ambiguous mailbox requests become exceptions.
The pilot covers one handbook and a limited set of personnel fields.
Build ranges include access and applicable consultation work; formal consultation may take longer.
The transformation-heavy prior fits records, while handbook approval remains substantive human work.
unknowns: Which fields have effective dates, audit trails and configurable validation in the {HCM}.
Whether personnel records and handbook documents share stable identifiers.
Which national consultation arrangements and retention schedules apply.
How many incoming changes lack valid approval evidence.
research_questions: Which handbook changes alter contractual obligations under the relevant national rules?
How should access and retention differ between personnel documents and published handbook versions?
new_work: Resolve rejected changes and conflicting effective dates.
Review handbook change maps and draft amendments.
Maintain field validation, access permissions and retention rules.
Investigate reconciliation failures and publication errors.
tasks.statement: Assist in preparing and maintaining personnel records and handbooks.

tasks.short: Prepare organisation charts, career paths and reports on job evaluation and compensation.

steps.what: Export position, reporting-line and compensation records for the reporting date.
Reconcile identifiers, effective dates, reporting lines and compensation definitions.
Build organisation charts, process diagrams, career paths and compensation tables.
Assemble findings, explanations and limitations around the charts and tables.
Check interpretation, confidentiality and audience suitability, then approve release.
Store the approved version and distribute access to the agreed audience.

tasks.design: A deterministic pipeline reconciles effective-dated records from the {HCM} and {PAYROLL} in the {DATA_PLATFORM}, then renders approved charts, tables and text templates into the {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} routes release approval and distributes audience-restricted links; the {BI} provides refreshable views using the same definitions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Identifiers, pay definitions and reporting dates did not align cleanly. Reusable reporting also required stable chart layouts and an approved career framework.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic validation, graph rendering and document templates cover most production work. AI-assisted coding can shorten adapter and template development without requiring generated interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: Matrix reporting, historical reorganisations and ambiguous career routes need clarification. A chart cannot establish that a career move is realistic or approved.
tasks.human_edge: Explain the organisational meaning of the results and catch reports that are numerically correct but misleading or too revealing.

ambition.what: A manager-facing career-path view showing approved moves and their stated requirements.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time rebuilding packs and more time explaining structural and pay anomalies. They can refresh approved views on demand; authority to change pay bands or career routes requires separate delegation.

reach.task: Reconcile compensation components used in HR reporting.
reach.learn: Distinguish contractual salary, paid earnings, allowances and full-time-equivalent measures.

reach.task: Connect approved career moves to learning pathways.
reach.learn: Express progression requirements as observable capabilities and identify unsupported routes.

evidence.claim: Reports and records are strong deterministic candidates; no task-specific product or outcome case is supplied.
Effective-date checks, chart rendering and template assembly require no model when inputs and conclusions are approved.
The digest discusses gender-neutral job evaluation, but its national legislative timing cannot be generalised across Europe.

assumptions: Job evaluation and substantive compensation analysis produce approved conclusions upstream.
Career paths and process diagrams are rendered from approved relationships rather than inferred from employee histories.
The main pack uses repeatable layouts; bespoke executive storytelling remains additional work.
Build ranges cover one reporting pack and a limited career-path view, including access and applicable national consultation.
GDPR applies to compensation reporting. This deterministic reporting design does not introduce AI-based worker evaluation.
unknowns: Available exports or interfaces and historical effective-date quality.
Definitions of salary, earnings, allowances and full-time equivalents.
Whether career routes and process maps are already approved and structured.
Audience permissions and rules for suppressing identifiable small groups.
Required report formats, languages and release approvers.
research_questions: Can chart rendering handle matrix reporting and large hierarchies legibly?
Which existing report and chart configuration can replace custom development?
Can reconciliation distinguish genuine compensation changes from timing and definition differences?
new_work: Resolve missing identifiers, reporting loops and compensation mismatches.
Maintain report templates and approved career relationships.
Review access groups and audience-specific suppression rules.
Check rendered layouts after structural changes.
Maintain calculation definitions and release records.
tasks.statement: Prepare reports, such as organization and flow charts and career path reports, to summarize job analysis and evaluation and compensation analysis information.

tasks.short: Administer employee insurance, pension and savings plans with brokers, providers and payroll.

steps.what: Collect employee changes and benefit elections.
Check eligibility, supporting documents and effective dates against plan rules.
Submit enrolments, amendments and cancellations to providers.
Reconcile provider confirmations, contributions and payroll deductions.
Resolve coverage and deduction exceptions with employees, providers and payroll.
Send benefit confirmations and correction instructions.

tasks.design: Configure change intake in the {HCM}, then use a rules service on the {DATA_PLATFORM} to validate eligibility and reconcile {PARTNER_PORTAL} confirmations with {PAYROLL} deductions. The {WORKFLOW} presents submission batches and correction instructions for approval, sends approved notices and retains receipts; unresolved coverage cases stay with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Provider formats, effective dates and plan rules differ. Interfaces and ongoing rule maintenance often cost more than the initial automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, scheduled jobs and configurable benefit events cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce connector and validation development time without changing eligibility rules.
tasks.still_hard: Retroactive coverage, disputed eligibility and provider corrections need judgement. Health data needs restricted access, and some providers may offer only manual portals.
tasks.human_edge: Protect coverage during difficult life events and negotiate a workable correction when provider and payroll records disagree.

ambition.what: Benefit continuity checks before extended employee leave

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from rekeying and reconciliation to coverage exceptions and preventive checks. The specialist can prioritise interventions; authority to change entitlements or plan terms does not expand automatically.

reach.task: Validate benefit deduction corrections before the pay run.
reach.learn: Deduction codes, payroll cutoffs and retroactive adjustment rules.

evidence.claim: Structured enrolment checks and contribution reconciliation suit rules, integrations and approval workflows; savings are estimates.
Significant solely automated entitlement decisions require assessment under GDPR Article 22.

assumptions: The first release covers one plan and one payroll population.
Approved plan rules can be expressed as effective-dated checks.
Supporting documents are checked for required evidence without sending medical details to a model.
Estimates include consultation under national rules where required; external waiting time may be longer.
unknowns: Which provider interfaces, exports and submission receipts are available?
Who may approve enrolments, cancellations and payroll correction instructions?
How many exceptions concern retroactive dates or disputed coverage?
Which employee consultation and access approvals are required?
research_questions: Can provider receipts identify acceptance at employee and effective-date level?
Which existing configuration can replace custom eligibility code?
new_work: Review submission batches and correction instructions.
Resolve unmatched records and rejected provider changes.
Maintain effective-dated plan rules and connector mappings.

Drafting from approved sources can reduce preparation, but instructional quality still needs specialist review.
The digest documents fabricated citations in a generated report, supporting explicit source checks for policy materials.

assumptions: The pilot covers one training programme and one language.
Approved policy versions and reusable course templates are available.
The time split retains substantial creative and teaching work, consistent with the supplied priors.
Build ranges are estimates, include applicable consultation work, and exclude unpredictable external waiting.
unknowns: Which enrolment, attendance and feedback features the current {LMS} supports.
Whether policy documents have reliable approval and version metadata.
Whether shift workers can access learning during paid working time.

Which national rules apply to mandatory training records and employee consultation?

Resolve unanswered questions from live sessions.
Refresh source mappings and exercises when policy changes.
Check that automatic completion records reflect actual participation.
tasks.statement: Plan and develop curricula and materials for training programs and conduct training.

tasks.short: Collect reliable evidence about jobs through surveys, observation, interviews and focus groups.

steps.what: Define research questions, participant groups and confidentiality arrangements.
Arrange sessions and send approved survey invitations.
Collect survey responses and follow up missing returns.
Observe employees performing representative duties and record contextual notes.
Interview employees and facilitate focus groups about responsibilities and working relationships.
Combine responses and notes into duties, requirements, relationships and unresolved differences.

loop.input: Approved survey responses and notes, with source identifiers and a job evidence schema.
loop.output: Source-linked duties, requirements, relationships and disagreements in a job evidence draft.
loop.check: Validate schema and source references; a specialist checks interpretation, omissions and minority accounts.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one repair per evidence pack; unresolved items become evidence questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Forms handle fixed fields, but narrative accounts describe the same duties differently and contain qualifications.

steps.what: Resolve disputed descriptions with participants and approve the evidence record.

tasks.design: Configure survey collection and scheduling in the {WORKFLOW}, {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}, with restricted evidence records in the {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop prepares source-linked job evidence; the specialist conducts observation, interviews and dispute resolution before approving the record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scheduling was straightforward, but fragmented notes and conflicting descriptions required substantial interpretation. Confidentiality also limited reuse.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and scheduling handle coordination. Bounded text extraction can now prepare a consistent evidence draft without deciding job value.
tasks.still_hard: Employees may describe formal duties rather than actual work. Trust, representative participation and disputes about responsibility still require direct contact.
tasks.human_edge: Notice hidden work, understand power differences and help employees describe duties without turning the discussion into a grading negotiation.

ambition.what: Include shift-based employees through short asynchronous job evidence submissions.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less scheduling and note assembly, leaving more time for observation and disputed roles. Within an agreed research remit, the specialist can commission targeted follow-up sessions; grading authority requires separate delegation.

reach.task: Improve role descriptions used in recruitment and onboarding.
reach.learn: Translate observed duties into clear requirements without copying incumbent characteristics.

reach.task: Design representative employee consultation.
reach.learn: Recognise participation barriers, confidentiality concerns and applicable national consultation rules.

evidence.claim: Forms, reminders and source-linked note extraction are feasible building blocks; task-specific performance is unproven.
If collected evidence feeds solely automated significant employment decisions, GDPR Article 22 requires assessment.
The digest documents Dutch works-council consent provisions; requirements elsewhere depend on national rules.

assumptions: Time shares describe specialist effort; employees' time completing surveys is additional.
Survey collection uses an existing form capability in the {WORKFLOW}; interviews and observation remain substantial.
The design summarises job evidence and does not score individual workers.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for one reusable collection process, including access and applicable national employee consultation.
GDPR applies; assess EU AI Act scope if the purpose extends to worker evaluation.
unknowns: Available survey, scheduling and document access capabilities.
Applicable national consultation rules and existing employee agreements.
Whether employees permit recording; the baseline design uses written notes.
Languages, shift patterns and accessibility needs of participants.
Who may access individual accounts and approve the evidence record.
research_questions: How accurately does extraction preserve disagreements and infrequent duties across the required languages?
Can existing form settings provide the required confidentiality and retention controls?
new_work: Review extracted evidence against the original accounts.
Handle missing responses and sensitive disclosures.
Maintain survey templates, access groups and retention settings.
Check that summaries do not erase minority accounts.
tasks.statement: Observe, interview, and survey employees and conduct focus group meetings to collect job, organizational, and occupational information.

tasks.short: Provide technical liaison on compensation and benefits with employers, public bodies and employee representatives.

steps.what: Locate correspondence, agreements, policy versions and relevant case facts.
Prepare a technical brief covering facts, open questions and the agreed mandate.

loop.input: Authorised source pack and explicit liaison mandate.
loop.output: Referenced brief separating established facts, disputed points and questions.
loop.check: Specialist checks every material assertion, source version and mandate limit.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved conflicts remain flagged for human handling.
loop.why_not_simpler: Correspondence and agreements express the same issue in varied language and may conflict.

steps.what: Arrange a discussion with the appropriate representatives.
Explain technical issues, hear concerns and discuss possible next steps within the mandate.
Draft the written response and record proposed responsibilities and deadlines.

loop.input: Specialist's discussion notes, referenced brief and proposed follow-up actions.
loop.output: Draft response and action register with unresolved commitments marked.
loop.check: Specialist checks attribution, deadlines, confidentiality and whether any promise exceeds the mandate.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; ambiguous agreements return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Discussion notes need interpretation to distinguish concerns, proposals and actual agreements.

steps.what: Approve and send the response, then register confirmed follow-up actions.

tasks.design: An authorised retrieval flow assembles the case pack from the {DOCS} and {EMAIL}; bounded loops draft a referenced brief and follow-up response. The specialist conducts the discussion, while configured scheduling and action tracking use the {CALENDAR} and {PROJECT}. The {EMAIL} sends substantive written commitments only after approval of the exact response.
tasks.previous_blocker: The value lies in trust, interpretation and authority to speak. Earlier tools could store correspondence but could not reliably prepare a case-specific brief.
tasks.enabler_now: Permission-aware retrieval and bounded drafting can reduce preparation and paperwork. Scheduling and action tracking can already be configured without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed interpretations, bargaining and institutional trust remain human. Sensitive correspondence needs purpose-limited access, and national rules determine representative consultation and negotiating authority.
tasks.human_edge: Read the counterpart's concerns, explain uncertainty honestly and know when a technical discussion is becoming a negotiation.

ambition.what: Pre-consultation technical issue clinic for employee representatives.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more of the week in substantive discussions and less assembling papers. The tool grants no additional negotiating or commitment authority; that must remain explicitly delegated.

reach.task: Prepare a joint issue register before a representative consultation.
reach.learn: Consultation procedure, bargaining mandates and how to distinguish clarification from commitment.

reach.task: Assess when a technical issue needs formal escalation.
reach.learn: Escalation thresholds, stakeholder interests and decision authority.

evidence.claim: Retrieval, controlled drafting and action tracking can support liaison work; the digest provides no direct liaison implementation case.
The conversation remains the largest time component; preparation savings do not imply automation of negotiation.

assumptions: The specialist normally works within an agreed liaison mandate.
Scheduling may send neutral invitations to selected contacts without disclosing the case pack.
Discussion notes are written by the specialist; recording or transcription is not assumed.
The relationship-heavy prior is retained, while preparation and follow-up remain open to automation.
Build estimates cover a pilot with selected authorised folders and one shared case process.
unknowns: Which counterpart relationships and types of commitments fall within the specialist's mandate?
Which cases require legal review or manager approval?
Where are authoritative agreements and correspondence stored?
Which national consultation rules and confidentiality arrangements apply?
research_questions: What confidentiality and retention rules apply to representative and government correspondence in the relevant jurisdiction?
new_work: Check source references and identify outdated agreements.
Review drafts for unintended commitments and inaccurate attribution.
Maintain authorised contacts, mandate limits and escalation rules.
Resolve missed deadlines and failed action-register updates.
tasks.statement: Consult with, or serve as, technical liaison between business, industry, government, and union officials.

tasks.short: Prepare compensation, benefits, or job analysis research for publication as reports, manuals, or learning material.

steps.what: Agree the audience, research question, publication format, and intended use.
Assemble research notes, approved data extracts, methods, and source documents from the {DOCS}.
Recalculate summary statistics and prepare publication tables and charts in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Interpret findings, challenge comparisons, and state methodological limits.
Write and format the manuscript, manual, or film script with citations and visual material.

loop.input: Approved findings outline, source documents, fixed tables and charts, and the publication brief.
loop.output: A formatted draft with claim-level source references and explicit limitations.
loop.check: Resolve every citation against the research pack. Compare all numerical claims with fixed results; flag unsupported claims for deletion or review.
loop.stop: One draft and at most two correction passes within a 15000-token budget. Unresolved claims remain flagged and block release.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates can place tables and headings, but varied audiences and research findings require new explanatory prose.

steps.what: Review substantive claims, confidentiality, and publication rights; approve the exact release version.
Publish the approved material through the {CMS} and archive the released version.

tasks.design: A controlled research pack in the {DOCS} feeds reproducible calculations and chart generation on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded drafting loop uses approved findings and traceable sources, while deterministic checks reconcile numbers and citations. The {WORKFLOW} captures approval of the exact release version before the {CMS} publishes it and the {DOCS} archives it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research publications were infrequent and varied in format, so bespoke automation was hard to justify. Manual copying connected calculations, prose, citations, and release approvals.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable calculation and publishing templates are cheaper to build with AI-assisted coding. Bounded drafting can adapt approved findings to an audience, while deterministic checks protect numerical consistency.
tasks.still_hard: Sound methods, defensible interpretation, disclosure risk, and editorial quality remain expert work. Small employee groups can remain identifiable after names are removed, and third-party research may restrict publication.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a useful question, distinguish evidence from speculation, and explain compensation findings without overstating fairness or causation.

ambition.what: An employee guide explaining job evaluation methods and their limitations.

tasks.altitude: During publication projects, the specialist spends less time copying figures and formatting drafts, and more time testing interpretations with readers. They can propose new publication formats; release authority remains with the authorised approver.

reach.task: Translate research findings into reward policy options.
reach.learn: How evidence quality, budget constraints, and employee effects shape a policy recommendation.

reach.task: Turn a research publication into employee learning material.
reach.learn: Learning objectives, accessible explanations, and checks that readers understand the method.

evidence.claim: Fixed analysis specifications support deterministic tables, charts, and reconciliation checks.
Approved sources and bounded drafting can reduce preparation work, but the digest contains no direct compensation-publication case.
A documented Australian government report case involved nonexistent sources and a partial refund, supporting direct citation verification.
Publication using employee research requires attention to GDPR purpose, access, and disclosure controls.

assumptions: This is an occasional supplemental task; reports and manuals are more typical than books or films.
The workflow ends with an approved release; a publisher submission can replace the {CMS} step.
The research dataset and analysis specification already exist. Designing and conducting a new study is separate work.
Film work here covers research content and script preparation, rather than full audiovisual production.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates. Low frequency may favour configuring templates before building integrations.
Consultation effort applies if employee-data use changes; access and rights checks apply to every implementation.
unknowns: The actual publication frequency, audience, formats, and release channels.
Whether existing analysis can be reproduced from retained source data.
Who approves scientific claims, employee-data disclosure, and external release.
Which source licences permit quotation, charts, or redistribution.
Whether the proposed data use requires employee consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which publication formats recur enough to justify reusable templates?
Which calculations and claim checks can run from a fixed analysis specification?
What disclosure thresholds are appropriate for the employee groups being described?
Would a manual template deliver sufficient value before adding a drafting loop?
new_work: Check generated prose against evidence and approved interpretations.
Maintain analysis specifications, templates, and citation checks.
Review disclosure risks and source publication rights.
Maintain release approvals, version archives, and correction procedures.
tasks.statement: Prepare research results for publication in form of journals, books, manuals, and film.

tasks.short: Design merit and incentive programmes, coordinate awards and prepare approved payroll changes.

steps.what: Export workforce, current pay, performance and budget data for the compensation cycle.
Reconcile employee identifiers, eligibility dates, currencies and pay components.
Model merit matrices, incentive formulas, budget costs and distribution effects.
Develop the programme proposal and discuss incentives, affordability and fairness with decision makers.
Approve programme rules and budget after required consultation.
Propose individual awards and justify departures from the approved guidelines.
Review award exceptions, budget totals and unexplained differences between comparable employee groups.
Approve final awards and documented exceptions within delegated authority.
Prepare approved award changes for payroll and check the import result.
Prepare award letters and distribute them through approved employee communication channels.

tasks.design: A governed job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles inputs from the {HCM}, {PAYROLL}, {TALENT} and {ERP}, then calculates programme scenarios for the {BI}. Configure proposal forms and separate programme and award approvals in the {HCM} and {WORKFLOW}. Only approved awards enter the {PAYROLL} change batch and populate fixed letters in the {DOCS}; payroll release retains its existing approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cross-system identifiers, changing pay components and local programme rules made integrations expensive. Choosing incentives and approving awards also requires accountable judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of building connectors, calculation tests and reconciliation views. Established compensation forms and approval workflows can handle the cycle without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Reliable comparators, incentive side effects and contested awards remain difficult. GDPR, equal-pay obligations and national employment and consultation rules constrain data use and changes.
tasks.human_edge: Anticipate how incentives change behaviour and defend fair, affordable choices to employees and managers.

ambition.what: A quarterly incentive-design review using actual costs and payout distributions.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from reconciliation and workbook repair to scenario discussions and exception resolution. With delegated authority, the specialist can convene quarterly design reviews and recommend adjustments; final budget and award authority stays with designated approvers.

reach.task: Evaluate incentive design against business objectives.
reach.learn: Behavioural effects, affordability and how to present competing programme options.

reach.task: Validate compensation changes before a pay run.
reach.learn: Effective dates, pay-component mappings and import reconciliation.

evidence.claim: Eligibility calculations, merit matrices, budget checks and approved-letter generation can use deterministic rules.
GDPR Article 22 requires assessment where individual pay decisions would be solely automated and significantly affect employees.
An AI system evaluating workers or affecting employment terms may fall within the AI Act's employment category; intended use needs assessment.

assumptions: The pilot covers one compensation cycle, currency and approved rule set.
Human managers supply performance judgements; the proposed solution does not generate worker scores.
Programme rules specify rounding, eligibility, effective dates and exception authority.
The creative and decision-heavy prior remains relevant despite substantial deterministic administration.
Build ranges include access and applicable consultation work; external approval timelines may exceed them.
unknowns: Whether the {HCM} includes configurable compensation planning and approval features.
Which pay components and identifiers agree across the {HCM} and {PAYROLL}.
Who has delegated authority for programme rules, budgets and individual exceptions.
Which employee comparison data can lawfully be used for distribution checks.
research_questions: Which incentive formulas create unintended behaviour under realistic operating scenarios?
Which national consultation and equal-pay requirements apply to programme changes?
Which validation controls detect incorrect effective dates and duplicate payroll changes?
new_work: Maintain eligibility rules and pay-component mappings.
Review reconciliation failures and unusual payout distributions.
Test rule changes against historical and boundary cases.
Check approval evidence and payroll import results.
Monitor actual incentive costs and behavioural effects.
